embryo-study-photo.kind: Original institutional photograph · early human-embryo research
embryo-study-photo.caption: A human blastocyst micrograph released by IOCB for the PCSK9/HBG base-editing study. Formation of this early structure is not evidence of safety during pregnancy or after birth.
embryo-study-photo.alt: A blastocyst micrograph showing the internal cell cluster and cavity
embryo-study-photo.credit: Štěpán Jeřábek · Columbia University / IOCB Prague
embryo-study-photo.changes: PNG converted losslessly to WebP; decoded pixels unchanged. No additional reuse permission is implied.

embryo-repair-source.caption: Left: DNA double-strand cutting. Right: single-strand nicking and base editing. The phrase efficient repair does not mean chromosome abnormalities or off-target changes are absent.
embryo-repair-source.alt: IOCB comparison of double-strand cutting by CRISPR-Cas9 and single-strand nicking with base editing
embryo-repair-source.credit: IOCB Prague · Adapted from Jeřábek et al., Nature, 2026
embryo-repair-source.changes: Original institutional PNG retained; interpretation is provided separately in the caption and article.

high-na-2024-source.kind: Official background image · early High-NA patterning, 2024
high-na-2024-source.caption: Early patterns made with CAR on the left and MOR on the right. This illustrates research infrastructure, materials, and metrology, not a 2026 large-mask prototype or volume-production result.
high-na-2024-source.alt: imec’s 2024 High-NA background image showing early CAR and MOR exposure patterns
high-na-2024-source.license: imec press and presentation image terms
high-na-2024-source.changes: Original JPEG; no cropping, compositing, or image alteration.

sulfide-film-fig2.kind: Original Figure 2 · film, cross-section, and elemental maps
sulfide-film-fig2.caption: Panels a–b show fluorine distributions; c shows film cross-sections and elemental maps; d shows a freestanding film; e compares the literature. A large fabricated sample does not establish continuous-production yield.
sulfide-film-fig2.alt: Complete original Figure 2 and caption: approximately 28 μm cross-section and a 30 by 10 cm freestanding film
sulfide-film-fig2.credit: Chunya Lou et al. · Nature Communications · 2026 · Figure 2
sulfide-film-fig2.changes: Full figure and caption extracted from page 5 of the early-release PDF; panels and lettering unchanged. Commercial or advertising use requires separate review.

sulfide-cycle-fig5.caption: Panel c: mold cell at 30°C, 1C, 2 MPa. Panel d: LTO-negative-electrode pouch cell at 40°C, 0.5C, 2 MPa. Capacity and coulombic efficiency use different axes. The 83% value is capacity retention after 1,000 cycles.
sulfide-cycle-fig5.alt: Complete original Figure 5 and caption showing voltage curves and long-term cycling of mold and pouch cells
sulfide-cycle-fig5.credit: Chunya Lou et al. · Nature Communications · 2026 · Figure 5
sulfide-cycle-fig5.changes: Full figure and caption from page 8 of the early-release PDF; no invented curves or rearranged panels. Commercial use requires separate review.

sulfur-source-fig1.kind: Original Figure 1 · theoretical comparison and reaction concept
sulfur-source-fig1.caption: Panels a–b explore theoretical specific energy, capacity, and voltage; c illustrates the sulfur oxidation-state pathway −2 → 0 → +1. Colors and stars are not measured pack performance or product certification. The complete figure is retained for discussion.
sulfur-source-fig1.alt: Original Figure 1 comparing theoretical energy, sulfur compounds, and the Li₂S-to-S₂Cl₂ reaction concept
sulfur-source-fig1.credit: Nan Zhang et al. · Nature Energy · 2026 · Figure 1
sulfur-source-fig1.license: Original copyright retained; limited reproduction for figure commentary
sulfur-source-fig1.changes: Publisher’s original PNG retained. No open reuse license is granted.

sulfur-crystal.kind: Sulfur-crystal background photograph · not a study sample
sulfur-crystal.caption: A sulfur crystal photographed in 2006. It is not the study’s S₂Cl₂, electrode, or prototype battery. It provides material context for readers new to sulfur.
sulfur-crystal.alt: Eric Hunt’s photograph of a yellow sulfur crystal, not a specimen from the reviewed study
sulfur-crystal.changes: JPEG converted to WebP with identical decoded pixels; no crop or composite.

sulfur-electron-range.caption: The horizontal axis is oxidation state per sulfur atom, not voltage, energy, or time. The two ranges differ by 2 and 3. The ratio 3/2 = 1.5 concerns electron count, not the measured 58% capacity increase.
sulfur-electron-range.alt: Illustration comparing sulfur’s −2 to 0 two-electron range with its −2 to +1 three-electron range
sulfur-electron-range.credit: JJo · Original educational calculation · English edition, September 13, 2026
sulfur-electron-range.changes: Labels translated from the original educational SVG; coordinates and accounting unchanged; no third-party figure reproduced.

sulfur-mass-basis.caption: Energy is fixed at a hypothetical 100 Wh while included mass changes from 0.1 to 0.5 kg. These are not the paper’s electrode or cell masses, and the chart does not convert its 1,700 Wh/kg result to pack performance.
sulfur-mass-basis.alt: At 100 Wh, dividing by 0.1 kg or 0.5 kg gives 1,000 Wh/kg or 200 Wh/kg
sulfur-mass-basis.credit: JJo · Original E/m teaching example · English edition, September 13, 2026
sulfur-mass-basis.changes: Labels translated from the original educational SVG; values and geometry unchanged; no external experimental curve reproduced.
